before.title: Heavy-load range collapse — 500-mile rating only on light freight
before.description: Tesla advertises 500 miles at 82,000 lb GCW, but real fleet deployment tells a different story. PepsiCo runs Frito-Lay (chips, ~light) Semis on ~425-mile routes, but limits Pepsi soda runs (heavy liquid loads) to ~100 miles before recharging. NACFE 'Run on Less' (Sept 2023) recorded one Semi needing a mid-day charge after 377 mi on a 545-mi day. Energy use averaged ~1.7 kWh/mi in DHL's October 2024 trial at 75,000 lb GCW.
before.solution: Route-plan around real-world ~1.7-2.0 kWh/mi consumption for heavy/dense freight, not the 500-mi marketing figure. Reserve Semis for sub-300-mi lanes that terminate at a Megacharger, and budget a mid-route 30-min charge for any run over ~350 mi at GCW.

before.title: Lithium-ion battery thermal runaway after crash — 50,000 gallons of water needed
before.description: On Aug 19, 2024 a 2024 Tesla Semi driven by a Tesla employee left I-80 near Emigrant Gap, CA, struck a tree, and the ~900 kWh pack went into thermal runaway. Battery temperatures hit ~1,000 F, fire/toxic smoke closed both directions of I-80 for 14-15 hours, and CAL FIRE used roughly 50,000 gallons (189,000 L) of water to cool the pack. NTSB opened HWY24FH015 — its first EV truck case.
before.solution: Train fleet drivers and first responders on Tesla Semi-specific emergency response (download Tesla's Semi ERG). Post-collision, do not attempt to move the unit — isolate, monitor pack temperature 24-48 hrs for reignition, and follow NTSB/NFPA Li-ion truck fire protocol.

before.title: Megacharger network gaps strand trucks off-corridor
before.description: The Semi is designed around 750 kW - 1.2 MW charging, but as of mid-2026 only a handful of public Megachargers exist (Ontario, CA opened Mar 2026; Tesla targeting 37 sites by EOY 2026, 46 by early 2027). Fleets running outside the I-5/I-10/I-75/I-95 corridors must build private depot chargers (~$1M+ per site) or accept that the truck is operationally tethered to its home base — not a long-haul OTR tractor in practice.
before.solution: Before ordering Semis, map every lane against Tesla's published Megacharger rollout and budget for an on-site DC fast charger (Tesla 750 kW Megacharger pedestal, ABB / Kempower MCS, or interim CCS1) plus the utility service upgrade — frequently the longest-lead item.

before.title: Parking brake valve module fails to engage — rollaway risk (NHTSA Recall 23V-205)
before.description: On 35 early-build 2023 Tesla Semi tractors, the Bendix-supplied electronic parking brake valve module (PVM) may fail to transition to the park position when the driver presses the parking brake button, due to excessive internal air leakage in the supplier's spec. If the service brake is released, the truck can roll away. No crashes reported, but a clear safety defect on a Class 8 unit.
before.solution: Free recall fix: Tesla Service replaces Bendix Intellipark Towing Park Brake Module (PVM) part 1124642-00-A with revised part 1124642-00-B that has improved internals preventing air leakage. Affects 35 units produced Nov 30 2022 – Feb 28 2023. Verify Recall 23V-205 / Tesla SB-23-33-001 is closed on the VIN before putting the unit in service.

before.title: Touchscreen flicker / shutdown forcing drivers to pull over
before.description: Consider removing the 'I-80' reference unless a specific source documents I-80 incidents — verified reporting centers on Modesto, CA (Frito-Lay facility) with units towed to Lathrop, CA. Both are in California's Central Valley, not on I-80.
before.solution: Keep the truck on the latest Tesla OTA firmware and report any flicker/blackout event to the Tesla Semi Service Program (Lathrop, CA) immediately. Tesla addresses these via software patch; mobile service can also reseat the display harness if the issue persists after an update.
